questions.stem: Newton's Third Law states that for every action there is:

options.text: A smaller reaction in the opposite direction
An equal reaction in the same direction
A larger reaction in the same direction
An equal and opposite reaction

questions.explanation: Newton's Third Law states that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction. The two forces are equal in magnitude but opposite in direction.

questions.stem: Newton's Third Law force pairs always act on:

options.text: Objects that are touching
The same object
Objects of equal mass
Two different objects

questions.explanation: Action-reaction force pairs always act on two different objects. This is why they do not cancel each other out.

questions.stem: When you push against a wall with a force of 50 N, the wall pushes back on you with a force of:

options.text: 0 N

questions.explanation: By Newton's Third Law, the wall exerts an equal and opposite force of 50 N back on you.

questions.stem: Why do Newton's Third Law force pairs not cancel each other out?

options.text: Because they are not equal in size
Because they act in the same direction
Because they act on different objects
Because one is always stronger than the other

questions.explanation: Forces can only cancel when they act on the same object. Third Law pairs act on different objects, so they cannot cancel.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a correct Newton's Third Law pair?

options.text: Air resistance on a car and the engine force
The weight of a book and the normal force from the table
Friction on a tyre and the weight of the car
Earth pulls the apple down and the apple pulls Earth up

questions.explanation: Earth pulling the apple down and the apple pulling Earth up is a true Third Law pair: same type of force (gravity), acting on different objects, equal magnitude, opposite direction.

questions.stem: A rocket launches by pushing exhaust gases downward. What is the reaction force?

options.text: Gravity pulling the rocket down
Air resistance pushing the rocket sideways
The weight of the fuel decreasing
The exhaust gases pushing the rocket upward

questions.explanation: By Newton's Third Law, the rocket pushes exhaust gases downward, and the gases push the rocket upward with an equal force. This is how rockets propel themselves.

questions.stem: Which property must Newton's Third Law force pairs share?

options.text: They must act on the same object
They must involve objects of the same mass
They must act at different times
They must be the same type of force

questions.explanation: Third Law pairs must be the same type of force (e.g. both gravitational, both contact). They act on different objects, in opposite directions, and at the same time.
